chunks.arabic_text: حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَعْبَدٍ عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا ع قَالَ

translations.en: My father, Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), saying:

chunks.arabic_text: شِيعَتُنَا الْمُسَلِّمُونَ لِأَمْرِنَا الْآخِذُونَ بِقَوْلِنَا الْمُخَالِفُونَ لِأَعْدَائِنَا فَمَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ كَذَلِكَ فَلَيْسَ مِنَّا

translations.en: Our Shia are those who submit to our command, accept our saying, and oppose our enemies; so whoever is not like that is not from us.

en.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Sifat al-Shia*, Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the essential criteria for authentic Shi'ism, emphasizing not just nominal affiliation but active submission to the Imams' authority and distinct opposition to their enemies. This definition underscores the concept of *Tawalli* (loyalty) and *Tabarri* (disavowal), which are foundational to Shia identity and theological practice. It serves as a practical litmus test for believers, linking doctrinal belief with communal allegiance and political stance.
en.seo_question: What are the three defining characteristics of true Shia according to Imam al-Rida?
